A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VLMFP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite reorganization and substantial additions in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original six-domain SimVLM and VLMFP experiments, component ablations, and unseen-rule evaluations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original 3D planning results, simulator comparisons, backbone evaluations, seed statistics, and failure and convergence analyses.

M1.justification: The dual-VLM architecture and generation, prescreening, consistency-checking, and refinement procedure remain intact. The 3D applications make a limited input adaptation: Assembly supplies initial and goal images, while MultiRob uses multiple views, enabling SimVLM to extract dependencies and occluded spatial relationships (Section 5.6; Appendix B.7).

E1.justification: v2 adds Assembly and MultiRob to the six retained grid-world domains. These introduce 3D assembly dependencies, image-specified goals, multiple robots, reachability constraints, occlusions, and multiple viewpoints (Section 5.6; Appendix A.1). The original appearance and FrozenLake rule-variation coverage remains.

E2.justification: Appendix B.1 adds systematic SimVLM comparisons with GPT4o-Direct and GPT4o-InContext across four output tasks. Appendix B.2 additionally compares LLaVA-NeXT-7B and PaliGemma2-10B simulator backbones. These substantially expand component-level comparisons; the end-to-end Direct, CoT, and CodePDDL comparator set in Table 2 is unchanged.

E3.justification: New 3D protocols collect 100k examples per domain and evaluate 1,000 simulator examples and 1,500 planning trials per appearance condition, with specified visual randomization and unseen color distributions. New backbone experiments vary model configurations. Appendix B.1 uses all-MiniLM-L6-v2 semantic similarity for GPT-4o execution reasoning while retaining exact matching for SimVLM, limiting direct comparability. The original grid-world protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds simulator-backbone sensitivity studies, quantified perception-versus-generation failure distributions, and refinement convergence measurements across six domains (Tables 7–8 and 12–13). These investigate dependencies and failure mechanisms beyond v1's component ablations and qualitative examples. The original component ablations and unseen-rule tests are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly reports means and standard deviations across three random seeds for all four SimVLM outputs, six domains, and both appearance settings (Tables 9–10). v1 reports averages over evaluation cases without seed-level uncertainty. The PDFs do not establish an increase from a specified earlier seed count.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 are unchanged, including VLMFP's 70.0%/54.1% grid-world success rates. New Table 5 reports Assembly success of 92.4%/85.9% and MultiRob success of 80.3%/73.6% for seen/unseen appearances. Further tables add simulator comparisons, backbone and seed results, error counts, and convergence rates. Table 13's reported averages, 77.1%/64.8%, conflict with its domain entries, which average approximately 73.3%/58.9%.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, generation and refinement equations, and Exploration Walk score in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. v2 adds empirical convergence measurements and implementation thresholds, but no new theorem, proof, or mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion now explicitly claim scalability to complex long-horizon 3D assembly and multi-robot planning under partial observability and visual variation. This substantially broadens the demonstrated applicability claimed in v1. The original autonomous dual-file generation and grid-world performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of simulator correctness without an external oracle, backbone independence, and perception failures in cluttered or visually unfamiliar scenes (Appendices B.2–B.3 and C.2). Appendix C.3 explains how an unconverged instance may still produce a reusable domain file. New discussion also proposes targeted error mitigation and temporal-image extensions, while retaining the earlier failure on entirely novel freezing dynamics.

D1.justification: Appendix C.3 supplies the previously omitted refinement prompt, a four-round refinement cap, numerical EW stopping tolerance, and behavior on nonconvergence. v2 also adds 3D input/output examples and states that code accompanies supplementary material, with public release planned. Existing fine-tuning hardware, hyperparameters, and the separate five-round prescreening limit are retained; these disclosures do not establish changes to those settings.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for the two 3D task sources and Qwen2-VL, LLaVA-NeXT, and PaliGemma2. The related-work positioning against methods requiring predefined domain files, human corrections, or environment interaction, and the central novelty claim, remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, tightens several explanatory passages, separates implementation details into Section 4, and reorganizes the appendix into parts A–E. It moves the unseen-rule descriptions and writing disclosure, and adds ethics, reproducibility, and acknowledgment sections. Most existing method and experimental prose remains recognizable and in the same narrative order.

P2.justification: v2 adds the 3D visualization in Figure 4 and eight tables covering 3D results, simulator comparisons, backbone tests, seed statistics, errors, and convergence. Original Tables 1–4 remain, and the old dataset-statistics Table 5 becomes Table 11. Existing figures are largely retained, with a corrected ice-hole precondition in Figure 2.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation beyond v1's grid-world evidence through 3D tasks, simulator comparisons, backbone sensitivity, seed statistics, and quantified failure analysis. The complete refinement prompt and stopping details also resolve important reproducibility omissions. These gains outweigh weaknesses in the additions: 3D results lack baseline comparisons, reasoning metrics differ between simulator comparators, and Table 13 contains inconsistent averages. The improvement comes from addressing validation and documentation gaps, while the original headline results remain unchanged.
